Verified closed on candidate sha256:3f51b79d671ebf6d220c5bb4b104916ca4eddac30266dd74c32e89ed37ccea4b (1455 files, recomputed in a complete clone at the freeze commit 1b8c158 and at the source 93a7dd7). The repairs are KBE-R5 and BE-R5.

1. Code (git diff a91d82c..93a7dd7):
- register.ts requirePermissionSomewhere now attaches denialOf(permission, target) after resolveTarget. An unknown transformation stays a plain 403 with no denial.
- The four separation-of-duties refusals carry .withDenial(denialOf(FINANCE_VALIDATE, ctx.target)): finance-validation.ts sod_submitter and baseline_validator_is_owner, overlaps.ts resolver_is_owner, valuation-methods.ts decider_is_proposer.
- tasks/routes.ts completeItem's work_item.not_assignee carries notAssigneeDenial (work_item.complete on the item's transformation or organization).

2. Probe S, round-2 form (probes/sec-dg4-r2-sweep.test.ts): the round-1 sweep with NO_DENIAL_OBSERVED emptied, and also failing any ADM-only or outsider 403 without a denial. Result: 766/766 passed, exit 0, ZERO [probe-S NO-DENIAL] lines. AUD: 406 calls, 308 x 403, each with exactly one authorization.denied; the rest are 96 x 400 (validation before authorization, nothing written) and 2 x 404 (markInboxNotificationRead). ADM-only: 126 x 403, each with its denial. Outsider: 106 x 403, each with its denial. No 2xx; the 201-table checksum is unchanged.

3. Probe D (probes/sec-dg4-r2-sod-denials.test.ts) exercises all four SoD refusals independently, each by a user who holds finance.validate. The repair's own slice-b-denials.test.ts covers only the first two. Each answers 403 with its SoD code and exactly one authorization.denied by the caller, reason '... requires finance.validate', and the target row is unchanged. 4/4, exit 0.

4. Probe E (probes/sec-dg4-r2-slice-b-ids.test.ts) checks that the added lookup discloses nothing. On createBenefit and decideFinanceValidation: a malformed id is 400 with no row; an unknown id is 403 with no row; an existing transformation is 403 with one denial (AUD); an org-B outsider is 403 with one denial attributed to the outsider. The three 403 bodies are byte-identical apart from per-request ids. 1/1, exit 0.

5. The repair's slice-b-denials.test.ts (7) and work-items.test.ts pass in both integration runs.

Residual, not a finding: an outsider's denial row is filed under org A's transformation. This is the platform-wide denials.ts design since DG2; probe C C6 shows the same for gate routes. The outsider cannot read it, and the response does not depend on it.

Verified closed on candidate sha256:3f51b79d671ebf6d220c5bb4b104916ca4eddac30266dd74c32e89ed37ccea4b.

1. Code:
- corrections.ts createCorrection now ends with stepOriginal. Under the same financeValidationQueue advisory lock (730233, lockQueue on the original measurement) and with the original locked FOR UPDATE by openTarget, it bumps the ORIGINAL finance_validation's version through bumpStamps with a version guard, and writes its own audit event finance_validation.corrected (prior/new version).
- openTarget still checks If-Match against the original's version, so the ETag now names the state of the whole correction chain.
- The worker's supersede path touches only queued items, so it is unaffected.

2. Migration 0061 is forward-only and contiguous. I diffed its function body against 0038's (the only other definition of finance_validation_guard): it is 0038 verbatim plus ONE branch. That branch admits an UPDATE only when OLD.kind = 'validation' AND OLD.status = 'approved' AND NEW.version = OLD.version + 1 AND every column except version/updated_at/updated_by is unchanged AND a correction row references it. The trigger is unchanged.

3. Probe F rev2 (probes/sec-dg4-r2-finance.test.ts; 10/10, exit 0):
- F2: FIN-B amends at If-Match 2 (201, 900). FIN-A's stale amend at If-Match 2 gets 409 version_conflict. The total stays 900.0000, no row and no audit row are written, and the original's ETag is now "3". In round 1 this case was 201 with the total 1100.
- F2a: stale amend, then stale reverse: the reverse is 409; total 800.0000.
- F2b: reverse, then stale amend: 409; total 0.0000.
- F2c: re-reading the original gives the fresh ETags 3 and 4, both accepted. The original keeps approved_amount 1000.0000 and its decider, and the three finance_validation.corrected rows chain 2->3, 3->4, 4->5.
- F3: amend and reverse concurrently at the same ETag: exactly one 201, the other 409.
- F3b: two concurrent amends: exactly one 201.
- F1 (one concurrent decision counted once), F4 (in-place edit 409) and F5 (900719925474099.1234 - 0.0001 exact) still pass.
- G, direct SQL as mth_app: version+1 combined with approved_amount, decided_by, status, content or reason; version+2; version-1; an uncorrected approved validation; a correction row; and a rejected validation are ALL refused by finance_validation_status_step. A bare version+1 (G1, G10) passes the 0061 guard but is refused at COMMIT by the 0010 finance_validation_audit_required trigger. With its audit event in the same transaction, G1 commits.

Residual, not a finding: G10, the 0061 branch, lets updated_by take any value. The app always sets the correcting user (bumpStamps), and the deferred audit rule still demands an audit row, so the correction itself cannot be fabricated.

Disclosure: probe F rev1 (probe-F-node22-lang-unset.log) exited 1 on G only. My expectation wrongly assumed that a bare SQL version step without an audit event could commit. Rev2 corrects only that expectation; F1-F5 are identical in both runs.

Verified closed on candidate sha256:3f51b79d671ebf6d220c5bb4b104916ca4eddac30266dd74c32e89ed37ccea4b.

1. Code: gates.ts writeAtCommit (updateGate, submitGate) first runs openWrite on the request-start grants, so the 404/403/422 refusals are unchanged. It then runs refreshPrincipal inside the write transaction, the read and write gates again on the reloaded grants, and commitTimeDenial. decideGate keeps its request-start read check (technicalAdminRefusal), then refreshes, and uses the reloaded principal for isApprover, the SoD check and the audit actor. Delegation (actsOnBehalfOf) and the delegator's grants are read inside the transaction.

2. The scanner (commit-scan6.py, unchanged) no longer lists the three gate routes as residual. 232 write routes, 33 residual, exactly round 1's other 33. Their source files are unchanged since round 1 (commit-time-residuals.txt).

3. Probe C rev2 (probes/sec-dg4-r2-gate-commit.test.ts; 6/6, exit 0). A change is made in the window after authentication with the implementers' afterIdentity helper:
- C1: a delegate decides G5 for the Sponsor. The control is 201. Revoking the delegation in the window gives 403 gate.not_approver, no decision, and one authorization.denied ('requires gate.decide').
- C2: the delegator's SP role is revoked in the window: 403 gate.not_approver with one denial.
- C3: the Sponsor's user is disabled in the window: 401, no decision, no audit row.
- C4: submitGate with the TL role revoked while an AUD grant keeps the read: 403, one denial 'requires gate.submit', no submission, gate row unchanged.
- C5: updateGate with the TO role revoked while AUD keeps the read: 403, one denial 'requires gate.configure', gate row unchanged.
- C6: an org-B outsider gets 404 on all three at request start, each with the read gate's one authorization.denied ('requires transformation.read'), as for every DG2+ route.

The repair's own gate-commit-time.test.ts (9) passes in both integration runs.

Disclosure: probe C rev1 (probe-C-node22-lang-unset.log) exited 1 on C6 only. My expectation of 'no audit row' for the outsider's 404 was wrong for this platform (denials.ts audits any unsafe-method problem that carries a denial, including the read gate's 404). Rev2 corrects only that expectation; C1-C5 are identical in both runs.

Residual, not a finding: as for every operation since DG3, the reload happens in READ COMMITTED inside the transaction, so a revocation that commits after the reload and before this commit is not seen.
